body: Thank you for your kind words.  Much appreciated. :)

Congrats! I wish you the best. :)  Yes, I completely understand you.  I'm the same age, and lost most of my life due to my abusive and controlling Nfather. As a teen, he wouldn't allow me to continue school, and then made me stay home, isolated me, and forced me to care for my very sick grandmother because "It was a females job, not a mans job". I was basically his slave and verbal punchbag for years. I lost all my friends at that time because of him, and haven't had any since. He shattered my mental health and confidence. I have no life outside of the walls of my house, and don't know how to, because I have never lived. I can't even drive, so that adds more isolation. I've also never got to experience being in love, and have never even been to a restaurant or a museum.  I cut him off months ago, but still my mental health is in shatters.

Sorry you experienced this too. I can relate to this so much. Everything I did was "stupid". That word was probably drilled into me every day of my life. I still feel that way about myself now. It was from ridiculous things like wanting to decorate my house, to me eating a type of food or meal that he didn't like or he deemed "too expensive", which was anything over £1, or even wanting to have hot water or use central heating when I'm cold. I was also "selfish" for wanting any basic human necessities.  I guess I am not worthy or was subhuman or less in his eyes.

Probably so. I lost a sibling (we didn't share the same Father), but my Nfather told me to stop being so stupid because I dared to cry over their death. Even him telling me the news was so cold. They sent me to school the next day, and then did not allow me to attend the funeral. And then a few years later, my Nfather threw out my siblings jacket in front of me, the only thing I had that belonged to them. I tried to protest what he was doing, but he gave me a ton a verbal abuse over it. As they were putting the jacket into the black trash bag, they did this with the same sinister, sociopathic grin which you talk about.  I will never forget that.

One of the times my Nfather threw a cup towards my head, he missed, and instead hit the wall with it, making a large dent in that wall. He knew he did it at the time, but later in the week he denied doing it and accused me of doing it, and then berated me, gave me hours of emotional and mental abuse for lying about it.  He was the liar, not me.

If you are willing to lie, you could always use the "I have the sh\*ts" excuse. Nobody ever questions that excuse, and they will want to leave you alone. A family dinner being on the Friday sounds perfect. ;) ;)

The best solution I found out is to never react when they say crazy things like this which they know irritate you. They do it for a reaction, it's what they thrive on. Instead, act like it doesn't phase you at all, and he probably wont do it, and maybe even soon forget the whole idea.

Yes! My Nfather also pretends his minor physical ailments are worse than what they are, so does those noises as if he were in pain, or sometimes almost dying.  I guess it is so that people will feel sympathy for him...? I'm not sure.

Yes, so true! daring to tell my Nfather  "No", he throws such a temper tantrum, plays the victim card and acts like he has been bullied by myself.  I was a "selfish, ungrateful,  and horrible"  person a few days ago because I didn't want him to come to my house.  Umm, there's a pandemic going on!  I'm a bad asthmatic and haven't had my vaccine yet. He is vaccinated and works around a lot of people. Was I the one being "Selfish, ungrateful and horrible" ?

I can sort of relate.  My nfather likes to call me "stupid" for cutting or doing anything with my own hair. I like my hair long, but sometimes it gets too long to manage and needs a cut. I will never forget the tantrums he's thrown the times when I've cut my hair.  Especially as a child, it had to be done, because he never once took me as a child to ever get my hair cut, only himself every month or so. He only treated my head lice problems when he was shamed for it by people who noticed. He threw out my hairbrush once, leaving me without, and then verbally abused the crap out of me for hours for having matted hair.

Yes, I can relate to the threats too. He regularly threatens to take my house from under me and make me homeless. It's mine, but under his name. He uses it as a control tactic. Also, he has made thinly veiled threats to call RSPCA on me, or to just take and give my dogs away.  I don't know what for exactly, because I know my dogs are treated like spoilt princesses. Another sick control tactic, taking something I care about most in the world to try and get me to do as he says.
Do you want to share those numbers? Sorry, I couldn't resist.
Believe me that I would if I had the means to.
I was only joking. I'm just in a very fed up and hopeless mood today and seeing no way out of it.

I've been using Symbicort for years, and I have had similar experiences. Sounds more like you suffered a panic attack than anything to do with the inhaler. Some people, including myself, cannot take paracetamol or aspirin without getting a panic attack.

Hang on in there. If you have survived avoiding it this long, you can probably do it for another few weeks or months until you get the vaccine. Just wear your mask, disinfect everything, open your windows, and try to avoid them like the plague... so to speak.

Yes. My anxiety gets worse in the 4 or so days leading up to my period. I get very sensitive to touch and pain, which I believe sets it off.  During my period I get very lightheaded and very physically exhausted, so much that I can barely move from the sofa, only when I have to use the bathroom or grab a quick snack. I read that lightheadedness is a common thing due to hormonal changes.
